$description: Peace Intel design tokens. DTCG-shaped. Every token carries a rationale and, where one exists, a machine-checkable constraint. The constraints are the point: an engineer who hits an accessibility problem can fix the value at the source instead of forking the palette in a page scope, which is what produced the two-brand split documented in audit/DRIFT.md.

$meta.rule: Token names match what production already spells. Adoption is a values swap, not a rename.
$meta.currentPreference: 2026-10-16, Rev 24: THE SANS IS BARLOW, at 0 tracking (DIN 2014 needed a paid web licence); --t-ui-ls is 0. 2026-10-16, Rev 22: THE TYPE SCALE OPENS UP: display 64px (was 46) and h1 48px (was 36), both at 400; body 16px (was 15), still --ink-70; the stat figure 72px. On screens up to 900px display is 44, h1 36, stat 48. NOTHING CASTS A SHADOW AT REST. 2026-10-16, Rev 20: TONE SETS BACK, THE EDGE MAKES AN OBJECT: --panel is renamed --ground, --panel-face --face, --panel-border --edge; --fill names the small set-back objects; --ground-2 (4%) is the console's sides and project page; --panel-elev is gone; the old names stay as production aliases. 2026-10-15, Rev 18: THE SERIF IS SOURCE SERIF 4, SET LIGHT: --serif-w 400 for every serif heading, --serif-w-display 500 at --t-display and --t-h1. Nanum Myeongjo and the Georgia hyphen face are gone. 2026-10-15, Rev 15: A BOTTOM GRID MASK (--grid-mask-bottom) for the console's chat. Hover stays a grey wash (a tint highlighter was tried and reverted the same day). 2026-10-15, Rev 13: THE SMALLEST TYPE IS 10px (the eyebrow ladder up a pixel). THE TIER MARKS ARE DRAWN by PI Marks, first in every font stack. The headline serif is under review (Nanum Myeongjo has no accented Latin). 2026-10-15, Rev 12: A MODAL DIALOG DIMS THE PAGE WITH --scrim, the shadow ink at a third. 2026-10-15, Rev 11: THE SEND BUTTON CARRIES THE CALL TO ACTION'S PIXEL ARROW, now the token --px-arrow drawn by both classes. THE TRAY'S RECESS IS THE PANEL TONE ON PAPER (a raised band keeps the shadow wash). Library titles take --t-ui-ls. 2026-10-15, Rev 10: THE TINT IS FINAL, a solid accent edge, twice the wash on a dark band, and an arrow. SEND WEARS THE TINT. UI ICONS ARE LUCIDE LINES (--glyph-ui 18px); PIXEL ICONS ARE ADOPTED for page content, as centred three-quarter squares (--px-screen); --glyph-px removed with the pixel send arrow. 2026-10-15, Rev 9: NO GRADIENT (--grad and --pi-grad removed). EVERY CORNER IS 4px. ELEVATION REFINED to a contact shadow plus a short ambient one. ONE ENTRY PRIMITIVE, .mo-deal (--mo-blur and --mo-in-lag went with focus and rule). TEXTURE IS FREE TO USE, never on two touching sections; mask-left and mask-right added. MORE THAN ONE DARK BAND per page is allowed. EVIDENCE BADGES ARE INK: the tint is for what can be clicked. --panel-sheer went with .card.sheer. --glyph-ui added for the console's glyphs. EARLIER: 2026-09-26, third pass — the decisions taken. THE GROUP REVEAL IS .mo-deal AND THE OTHER FOUR ARE DELETED (.mo-unmask, .mo-stagger, .mo-cascade, .mo-uncover). CORNERS ARE SCROLL-LINKED off the same --reg progress as registration, with their own --cnr-* tokens, and a card wears AN EDGE OR CORNERS, NEVER BOTH. RADII STAY AT 2/4; the third step of 6 was built and rejected. THE GRADIENT CTA IS BACK as .btn.grad, the one control allowed to wear --grad, with a WHITE label as of 2026-10-08 (color.on-grad), a knowing contrast exception recorded on that token. THE FIELD RAMP ENDS AT --line-2 (14%), not --wash-1: three percent was past quiet into invisible. A ROW OF SEPARATED ITEMS TAKES ONE RULE, ON TOP. SECOND PASS, 2026-09-25, still stands:  THE DITHER CELL IS 3 AND IT IS MEASURED: run lengths in the original dove and looking-glass masters give two source pixels at a 720px width drawn across a 1120px stage, so everything derived from them had been running about twice as fine as the brand's own assets; the masters were copied in rather than re-derived. GRADIENT FIELDS SPAN --bg TO --line-2 (fourteen percent of ink, five stops, corrected 2026-09-26 from three percent, which was past quiet into invisible) AND ARE ALWAYS LIVE, because a still field at any of these weights is just uneven paper. --panel-face SPLITS A RAISED COMPONENT FROM A RAISED REGION, because a card at --panel on a band at --panel is one tone used twice; a raised surface moves away from the page toward the light, which is white in light mode and lighter in dark. VIDEO IS MONOCHROME IN LIGHT AND WARM IN DARK, where it reads as thermal and the dove reads as infrared, and a clip with no white ground goes edge to edge or not at all. THE GRADIENT MOVED TO Pl. 01 with the colours: it is a brand asset, not a component. All four of that pass's open questions were answered on 26 Sep and are recorded above; the five unadopted surface approaches in Pl. 15 stay as the record of what the edge was weighed against. FIRST PASS, the same day, still stands:  CORNERS ARE 2 AND 4, reversing the square decision of 24 Sep: 2px for small things whose whole silhouette is the corner, 4px for anything with an interior, --r-full restored for things that are actually round. EVERYTHING LIGHTENED: raised wash 3% → 2%, --line .12 → .08, --line-2 .18 → .14, elevations down about a third. WARM IS A COLOUR, NOT A SURFACE: .surface--warm removed, three uses only (callouts, violators, the gradient-field ramp). THE ACCENT SPLIT GAINED A THIRD TOKEN: brand orange has no legible text colour on it (4.29:1 under white, 4.33:1 under ink), so a filled accent control writes --accent-fill plus --on-accent; the red-to-orange gradient button is gone (see the gradient, now in Pl. 01). GRADIENT FIELDS ARE MONOCHROME and render at --dither-cell; one cell governs the fields, the clips, the rendered grid and the motion primitives. MOTION RETIMED to 900–1600ms for entries, .mo-sweep removed, .mo-develop / .mo-focus / .mo-rule / .mo-unmask added. REGISTRATION IS ONE OF EIGHT MOUNTS and never on a full-width element. VIDEO SPLIT into .veil (a subject on a seamless, atmosphere, no box, sits behind type) and .vmap (footage that fills its frame, a figure, mapped and mounted). Typefaces unchanged: Nanum Myeongjo / DIN 2014 / Space Mono. Rev 4 is frozen at handoff/archive/ if it is needed for comparison.
$meta.measuredAgainst: --pi-paper-100, the warm primitive the ink ramp was solved on, which is darker than every surface text sits on. On --ground-2 (4% ink), the darkest of those, --ink-55 measures 4.76:1.
$meta.source: tokens.css is the source of truth. Every token names its CSS variable in $extensions["pi.css"], semantic tokens alias primitives with {group.token} references exactly as the CSS aliases them with var(), pi.resolved is the value as the browser renders it in light, and pi.modes lists every context that redeclares the token (dark, onDark, raised, invertInDark, onDarkInDark). Generated against tokens.css on 2026-10-08 and checked by guide.html, which reads both files and reports any drift.

changes: motion.sheet (--mo-sheet, 320ms decelerating): the phone's library sheet, Rev 31.
font.sans: Barlow replaces DIN 2014 (SIL OFL, self-hosted, true 600).
The --t-ui-ls tracking token is 0em (was .02em, a DIN correction).
typeScale.display 46px -> 64px, lineHeight.display 1.24 -> 1.06; typeScale.h1 36px -> 48px, lineHeight.h1 1.24 -> 1.1 (headline to body about 4x).
font.serif-w-display 500 -> 400 (Matt: with the larger size, set it at 400).
typeScale.body 15px -> 16px, lineHeight.body 1.65 -> 1.6; body stays --ink-70.
component.t-stat 48px -> 72px, so the stat figure stays larger than display.
color.panel renamed color.ground (--ground); color.panel-face renamed color.face (--face); surface.panel-border renamed surface.edge (--edge).
Added color.ground-2 (--ground-2, 4% ink) and color.fill (--fill).
Removed surface.panel-elev (always none).
color.panel, color.panel-face and surface.panel-border kept as aliases with pi.deprecated, for production's console.css.
Rule kept for every other token: names match what production spells. This is the one rename, and the aliases make it a values swap still.
font.serif is Source Serif 4 (was Nanum Myeongjo); PI Serif Hyphen removed from the stack.
Added font.serif-w (--serif-w, 400) and font.serif-w-display (--serif-w-display, 500). Every serif weight in the system is one of the two.
Added texture.mask-bottom (--grid-mask-bottom) for .textured--bottom.
color.wash-tint, a hover highlighter, was added and removed the same day (Rev 16): hover stays --wash-1.
typeScale eyebrow ladder up one pixel: eb-1 13px, eb-2 12px, eb-3 11px, eb-4 10px. Nothing is set under 10px.
font.serif, font.sans and font.mono start with PI Marks, an inlined three-glyph face (U+25CF, U+25D0, U+2197) that draws the tier marks.
Added surface.scrim (--scrim, rgba(var(--sh), .32)), what a modal dialog dims the page with: the console's context, memory, instructions and note dialogs.
Added component.px-arrow, the 3 x 5 chevron .btn.tint::after and .send::after draw.
Added letterSpacing.ui (--t-ui-ls, .02em), for a run of titles at 13px.
surface.tray is {color.panel} on paper; a raised band restates the shadow wash; the dark-band value is unchanged.
Removed component.glyph-px: the send glyph is a Lucide line now.
component.glyph-ui is 18px: a line icon, not an 11-cell pixel glyph.
Added component.px-screen, the adopted pixel-icon mask.
component.icon-px adopted rather than held.
Removed color.grad and primitive.grad: no gradient, for now. Breaking for anything that read --grad.
Removed color.panel-sheer with .card.sheer, which no page used.
Removed motion.blur and motion.in-lag with .mo-focus and .mo-rule; .mo-deal is the one entry primitive.
radius.xs and radius.sm are 4px: every corner is 4px.
elevation 1 to 3 refined, quieter and shorter, with their dark-band values listed as onDark modes.
Added texture.mask-left and texture.mask-right, and component.glyph-ui (22px).

Dark mode removed (Matt: too heavy and intense for the brand). Every dark, invertInDark, raisedInDark and onDarkInDark mode is gone, with the color.dark group and the primitives dark-000, dark-100 and orange-bright, which only the dark theme used. Dark bands (onDark) are unchanged. Breaking for anything that read a dark value.
color.on-grad removed with the gradient button: every call to action is now .btn.tint, which needs no label token. The gradient itself (--grad) stays as a brand colour.
New surface.tray, the recess of the tray that every choice among options now sits in (.pills.tray, .seg).

component.icon-px is 50px, from 51px: page icons moved from 17 cells at the 3px dither cell to 25 cells at 2px, picked by Matt in the 9 October review because strokes broke up at 17. Still HELD with the icons. glyph-px is unchanged and stays on the dither cell.
No token changed for the rail mount, cut the same evening; it used spacing tokens only.
Removed the registration and corners groups and --mount-recess, cut with .reg, .mount--corners and .mount--recess. Breaking for anything that read them; they survive only in archive/retired.css.
New --gridink: the light-page grid by name, so an inverted light band on a dark page shows its grid.

The seven composed tokens are restated inside .on-dark and .surface--invert, so their pi.warning entries are gone: --hl, --link-h, --elev-1/2/3 and --panel-sheer now compose from the band they sit in. --mount-recess, the seventh, was cut.
A light band on a dark page takes the 2% wash as its panel, not the retired warm #F3EFE7.
Radius: pills, chips and radio pills moved from --r-md (4) to --r-sm (2). No value changed.
Motion prose no longer lists .mo-settle, cut as unused on every shipped page.
component.icon-px and component.glyph-px marked HELD: the pixel icons are not adopted, and .px-icon and .points moved to explorations.css. No value changed.

No new tokens. The Rotary and Home blocks adopted into components.css this round (.stack, .sec-head.wide, .ledger, .fig-split, .scrolly, .checks, .orgs and the screen shapes) all compose existing tokens.
New component.icon-px and component.glyph-px, added with handoff/home.html and the pixel-icon pass in media/mkicons.cjs.
font.serif leads with PI Serif Hyphen, a hyphen-only local Georgia face, so compounds in serif headings stop reading as dashes.
Gradient button label is white: new color.on-grad (#FFFFFF), a recorded contrast exception. Reverses the ink label of 2026-09-26.
Every token carries pi.css. The name mapping no longer has to be guessed.
New primitive group (18 tokens), mirroring Layer 1 of tokens.css. Semantic colours now alias primitives rather than repeating hex.
Added the 59 variables tokens.css declared and this file did not, including line heights, eyebrow tracking, component tokens, corners and texture.
Removed motion.sweep, motion.resolve and motion.register: the first two named primitives and timings deleted on 2026-09-25, the third is a behaviour, now recorded on the registration group.
registration.internal / clear and media.tier-* kept as pi.kind "rule": documented rules with no CSS variable.
Values synced to the CSS: motion durations record their easing; layout.bandY aliases space.26; elevations reference color.sh.
Seven composed tokens flagged with pi.warning because they do not follow .on-dark or .surface--invert: --hl, --link-h, --elev-1/2/3, --panel-sheer, --mount-recess.
Corrected prose that contradicted the current system: the motion primitives list, the surface description and the registration rule paths.

primitive.$description: Layer 1. Raw values. No component references these directly; semantic tokens alias them.

paper-000.$description: Warm paper. The page tone in light.

paper-100.$description: Warm paper, one step down: the warm tone and the old raised fill.

$extensions.pi.note: raised, warm (default)

ink-900.$description: Near-black ink. Primary text in light, and the fixed label on an accent fill in dark.

ink-600.$description: Secondary ink. Solved against --pi-paper-100 so it clears AA on page and raised surfaces.

ink-400.$description: Muted ink: the AA floor for body text on a raised surface.

ink-300.$description: Line and disabled ink. Not a text colour (3.11 to 3.34:1).

dark-band.$description: A dark band inside a light page.

$extensions.pi.note: a dark band inside a LIGHT page

dark-300.$description: Line and disabled ink on dark surfaces. Not a text colour.

orange.$description: Brand orange. Graphics, large type and fills; 4.18:1 on the page, so never small text in light.

orange-text.$description: The darker orange that clears AA for text under 24px on page and raised surfaces.

$extensions.pi.note: AA on both page and raised surfaces

orange-warm.$description: The accent on a dark band inside a light page, and on an inverted ink chip.

bg.$description: Page and card background. Warm off-white, never pure white.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The warm cast is the whole basis of the brand's depth. Chosen over a cooler blue variant in an A/B on 2026-07-08.

ground.$description: A region set back from the page: a band (.surface--ground), the recess a choice sits in. Two percent of ink. Was --panel until 2026-10-16.

$extensions.pi.rationale: RESOLVED 2026-09-24, lightened 2026-09-25. A raised surface is a hairline PLUS a very light wash: the edge defines, the wash gives body, and neither does the other's job. The warm #F3EFE7 this token used to hold is now --warm, a colour with three uses rather than a surface. Three percent read as a different colour rather than as the same paper lifted; two is where the edge does the identifying.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Do not raise above 3%. Past that a band of it stops reading as the page.
$extensions.pi.scope: RENAMED 2026-10-16 (Rev 20). TONE SAYS SET BACK, THE EDGE SAYS OBJECT. The tone was --panel, a name that means a raised board, while the console used it as a background. --ground is a region; an object on it reads --face; a small object that is itself set back (a badge, an avatar, the user's bubble) reads --fill.

ground-2.$description: A region set further back: the console's rail, library and project page (.surface--ground-2), so the conversation is the brightest thing on screen. Added 2026-10-16.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Matt, 2026-10-16: a slightly darker background for the left sidebar, right sidebar and project page. The darkest tone text sits on, so it is capped by --ink-55: 4.76:1 at four percent, 4.52:1 at six.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Do not raise above 5%. Console only; marketing pages use --bg and --ground.

face.$description: The face of an object on a ground: a card, a library entry, the open chat in the rail. The page tone in light, the ground tone on a dark band. Was --panel-face.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Added 2026-09-25 after light mode read heavy. A RAISED SURFACE MOVES AWAY FROM THE PAGE TOWARD THE LIGHT, and that direction is opposite in the two themes: whiter on paper, lighter on near-black. Dark mode was already doing this; light mode was not, so the rule existed as an exception. One token makes it one principle. In light the inside of a card is white and the hairline does the raising.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Inside .surface--raised it returns to --bg in light and steps to 6% ink in dark, so a card stacked on a raised region still separates. Six alternatives to the hairline-plus-white default are laid out in Pl. 15 and none is adopted.

fill.$description: A small object that is itself set back: a badge, an avatar, the user's own message. The ground's tone at object size. Added 2026-10-16.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Each is meant to be quieter than what is beside it (the question is quieter than the answer), which is the ground's meaning at object size. Named apart so a component says which job it is doing, and so the two can diverge without a hunt.

panel.$description: FORMER NAME, kept for production's console.css only: now --ground. Nothing in handoff/ may use it; remove once production reads the new name.

panel-face.$description: FORMER NAME, kept for production's console.css only: now --face. Nothing in handoff/ may use it; remove once production reads the new name.

ink.$description: Primary text. Warm near-black. Also the fill for inverted elements.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Opaque, not alpha. The prototype's alpha inks composited below AA; production flattened them for the same reason. Opaque values can be tuned against a target; alpha values drift with whatever surface they land on.

The AA floor for body text. Solved against --panel, not --bg: an earlier revision measured 4.52:1 on the page but only 4.04:1 on a raised surface, so every piece of muted text on a card or a chat bubble was silently failing.

ink-35.$description: Faint text: timestamps, section markers, disabled states. Also hover border colour.

$extensions.pi.rationale: 3:1 is the WCAG floor for UI components and large text. Anything fainter cannot carry meaning.

Borders stay alpha deliberately. They sit on --bg and --panel alike and must composite against both. Production flattened this to #e2e0da, which is correct on --bg and slightly wrong on --panel. Lightened from .12 on 2026-09-25: the system had drifted heavy, and a page of twelve cards was twelve announcements. A hairline should be the thing you notice only when it is missing.

line-2.$description: The edge of anything a person can act on: a card, an input, a pill.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Lightened from .18 on 2026-09-25 with the rest of the system. It stays heavier than --line on purpose.
$extensions.pi.constraint: FLOOR .12. WCAG 1.4.11 asks that a control be identifiable, and an input whose boundary you have to hunt for is a worse failure than a border slightly darker than the divider beside it.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Separate from the text ramp so the opaque inks can be tuned for contrast without breaking hover states.

accent.$description: The one brand accent. Graphics, large type, fills, focus rings.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Used for meaning only: evidence, primary action, focus, active state. More than three or four accented spots in a view means it is over-accented.
$extensions.pi.warning: 4.18:1 on the page FAILS AA for text under 24px — use accent-text. It ALSO fails as a FILL: white on #D9481C is 4.29:1 and ink on it is 4.33:1, so there is no legible text colour on brand orange in either direction. A filled accent control uses accent-fill plus on-accent.
$extensions.pi.openQuestion: The original brief specified an EPI green accent. The prototype supersedes it with warm orange. Flagged for the board, not silently resolved.
$extensions.pi.decided: 2026-09-24 — warm orange is the accent. No second accent is carried.

accent-text.$description: Accent for any text under 24px. AA guaranteed.

$extensions.pi.rationale: A barely perceptible darkening of the brand orange that clears AA on BOTH the page and any raised surface. This is what makes the brand value usable for body text without adopting a different hue.

accent-fill.$description: The BACKGROUND of a filled accent control. Always written together with on-accent.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Added 2026-09-25, and it is the other half of the accent split. The split solved orange as a FOREGROUND and left orange as a BACKGROUND unsolved: #D9481C measures 4.29:1 under white and 4.33:1 under ink, so a solid orange button with 14px type failed AA whichever way you turned it. On light the fill steps down to the darker orange that already existed for text (5.26:1 under white). On dark the accent is already lighter, so the fill stays and the TEXT goes to ink (6.66:1 on the on-dark accent, 5.49:1 on the dark-theme one); white on those is 2.79 and 3.38 and was the worst failure on the page.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Never write --accent as a background with a literal white on it. Write the pair.

on-accent.$description: Text on accent-fill. Flips to ink on dark surfaces, where the fill is the bright accent.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The only legitimate pure white in the system on a light page, and it is not white at all on a dark one. It moves with accent-fill; the two are one decision.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Must derive from accent. Production hardcodes rgba(217,72,28,.14), which disagrees with its own brown accent.

onDark.$description: A dark band or card INSIDE a light page (.on-dark), and the light-on-dark direction too (.surface--invert flips against the theme). Neither codebase had this layer; both hardcoded white-alpha, which meant dark bands inverted into light bands the moment a dark theme was applied. The ramp is solved against #211D16, the LIGHTER of the two band surfaces, so one ramp serves both a band on a light page and a band on a dark page.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Replaces a hardcoded #1C1A16 that was a fourth near-black with no token, distinct from --ink.
$extensions.pi.note: Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The light-mode accent measures only 4.05:1 on this surface, so the band needs the warmer end of the gradient.
$extensions.pi.note: Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
Declared only inside .on-dark and light-page .surface--invert; it has no value at the root.
With ink on it. White on it is 2.79:1 and was the worst failure on the page.

accent-on-ink.$description: The accent on a slab of --ink, the one surface that does not flip with the theme, so the accent on it moves the opposite way to everything else.

$extensions.pi.note: --ink is light inside a dark band

kicker.$description: Eyebrow colour. Aliases --ink-55, so one knob controls every kicker.

sh.$description: The shadow colour as an RGB triplet, so each elevation layer can set its own alpha.

serif.$description: Editorial voice: headlines, card titles, entry titles. Source Serif 4 since 2026-10-15, set light.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Replaced Nanum Myeongjo, whose Latin had no accented letter, so French headings were set partly in Georgia. Source Serif 4 covers French, the European languages and Vietnamese, and its optical sizes give a 46px headline the display cut automatically. The Georgia hyphen face (PI Serif Hyphen) that patched Nanum's wide hyphen was removed with it.
$extensions.pi.note: Load it with opsz and a 400 to 600 range: family=Source+Serif+4:ital,opsz,wght@0,8..60,400..600;1,8..60,400..600

serif-w.$description: The weight of every serif heading. Nothing serif is bold.

serif-w-display.$description: The serif at the two largest sizes, --t-display and --t-h1 (and the stat number above them). 400 since Rev 22, 2026-10-16 (was 500): at 64px the size carries the weight. The token stays so the two can still differ.

$extensions.pi.note: Barlow since 2026-10-16 (Rev 24), replacing DIN 2014, which needed a paid web licence. SIL Open Font License; self-hosted in Fonts/Barlow/ (400, 400 italic, 500, 600, 700; Latin, Latin Extended, Vietnamese) with OFL.txt. DM Sans is the fallback.

mono.$description: Instrument labels: kickers, timestamps, citation chips, badges.

$extensions.pi.note: Every stack starts with PI Marks (2026-10-15), an inlined three-glyph font restricted to U+25CF, U+25D0 and U+2197, so the tier marks are drawn the same on every device. Source: Fonts/PIMarks.woff2.

$extensions.pi.decided: 2026-10-16 — Source Serif 4 / Barlow / Space Mono. Source Serif 4 replaced Nanum Myeongjo on 2026-10-15; Barlow replaced DIN 2014 on 2026-10-16. DM Sans remains the sans fallback.

typeScale.$description: Ten steps. Replaces 32 ad-hoc sizes found in problems.html and 25 in rotary-a.html.

$extensions.pi.constraint: A font-size that is not a step here is a bug. Add a step before using a new value.

eyebrow.$description: Four ladder steps for mono uppercase labels. Replaces thirteen letter-spacing values plus three in raw pixels. Tracking scales inversely with size.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Do not invent new size/tracking pairings. Use a step.

$extensions.pi.use: section kickers
nav, pane titles, stat labels
badges, timestamps, action buttons
micro labels, source-type suffixes

eyebrow-1.$description: Tracking for eyebrow step 1. Tracking scales inversely with size.

$extensions.pi.note: section kickers

eyebrow-2.$description: Tracking for eyebrow step 2. Tracking scales inversely with size.

$extensions.pi.note: nav, pane titles, stat labels

eyebrow-3.$description: Tracking for eyebrow step 3. Tracking scales inversely with size.

$extensions.pi.note: badges, timestamps, action buttons

eyebrow-4.$description: Tracking for eyebrow step 4. Tracking scales inversely with size.

$extensions.pi.note: micro labels, source suffixes

ui.$description: Tracking for a run of titles at --t-ui (library entries, document names). 0 since Rev 24: it was .02em because DIN closed up at 13px, and Barlow is set at 0. Never for body copy.

space.$description: 4px grid. The prototype had no spacing scale at all (DESIGN-TOKENS.md §8 says so) and grew to 24 distinct margin values in one page.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Every margin, padding and gap is a step here. Nothing off-grid.

radius.$description: RESOLVED 2026-10-15: ONE CORNER, 4px. It was two steps from 2026-09-25 (2px for small things whose silhouette is the corner, 4px for anything with an interior; a third step of 6 was built and rejected on 2026-09-26). Matt made every corner 4px on 2026-10-15: one answer is one fewer place for two components to disagree, and a chip and the button beside it read as one family. The six names survive so a component keeps the name that says what it is and adoption stays a values swap. --r-full is for genuinely round things.

$extensions.pi.use: focus ring
citation chips, badges, violators, pills, chips
buttons, inputs
cards, chat bubbles
composer, hero surfaces
CTA band
avatars and status dots: round things are round

elevation.$description: Warm-tinted via --sh, always a tight contact shadow plus a soft distant one.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Elevation signals interactivity. Static content gets borders, not shadows.
$extensions.pi.rationale: REFINED 2026-10-15 (Matt: more subtle and refined), after being lightened by a third on 2026-09-25. Each step is a one-pixel contact shadow that gives the edge a foot plus a short ambient shadow pulled in by a negative spread so it never shows past the sides: paper resting on paper. The old elev-3 threw 34px at .32.

$extensions.pi.use: a hovered card, a chosen tray tile, a hovered chip
the prompt and the console at rest
the prompt and the composer under focus

$extensions.pi.constraint: Animate only box-shadow, border-color, background, transform, filter, mask and opacity. No bounces, no springs. INTERACTION motion (hover, focus, press) stays under .3s. ENTRY motion runs 900–1600ms, revised 2026-09-25: a reveal that finishes before the eye arrives at it did not happen, and the old 320–520ms range made the signature move of the system invisible. Always ship the reduced-motion kill switch, and gate every hidden start state behind [data-js].
$extensions.pi.language: 'Resolve, don't type.' No typewriter, terminal cursor, redaction bars or scanlines; those are costume. The primitives: .mo-resolve (the signature, content emerging through clearing dither), .mo-develop (tone coming up to density — the only one safe on a block of copy, because text that fades in from transparent flickers and text that comes up in contrast does not), .mo-focus (soft then sharp; figures and imagery, never type), .mo-rule (a hairline draws, then the content writes in under it — the default for a section head), .mo-deal (the group reveal and the only one: a mask per child, staggered, each rising six pixels) (a measurement arriving, damped, never overshooting), and .reg (scroll-linked registration, see the registration group). .mo-sweep was REMOVED on 2026-09-25: a raking pass of light was the one primitive with no counterpart in the work, and on a real card it read as a loading skeleton, which is a promise that data is coming.
$extensions.pi.chosen: DECIDED 2026-09-26: .mo-deal is the group reveal and the only one. It goes on the CONTAINER and the children move — a soft mask per child, staggered, each rising six pixels under it — and nothing else in the set touches children. The other four are DELETED from components.css rather than left in as options, because a motion set with five ways to do one thing has no grammar and an unadopted primitive is an adopted primitive eventually. The record, so the decision is recoverable: .mo-unmask treated the block as one object with no opacity change anywhere and said nothing about the order inside it; .mo-stagger carried the order but faded each item, and a fade at 10px mono is a flicker; the three syntheses asked whether the sequence could be carried by the mask instead of by opacity, with .mo-cascade timing children to one travelling edge, .mo-uncover giving every child its own mask, and .mo-deal adding the rise. The property lost with uncover is worth naming: it changed no opacity anywhere, which made it safe on 9-10px mono at any count. Deal moves the item rather than fading it, so type is still at full density from its first visible frame. Compared on a card and on a citation list in Pl. 10, which is where the count is high enough for the difference to show.
$extensions.pi.safety: Every hidden starting state is gated behind [data-js] and backed by a 2.5s reveal timeout. Animation is never load-bearing for legibility.
$extensions.pi.twoScales: TWO SCALES, because they are two different jobs. INTERACTION (--mo-fast/base/struct) is a control answering a click and stays under .3s; past that the interface feels like it is thinking. ENTRY (--mo-in-1..5, added 2026-09-25) is an element arriving as you scroll to it and runs 700–1600ms. Five steps rather than three because a reveal usually has two parts moving at different rates — content and the noise over it, a line and the text under it — and matched durations flatten the two layers into one crossfade. The gap between steps is what makes layers legible as layers.

surface.$description: Tone sets back, the edge makes an object (renamed 2026-10-16). A region is color.ground (2% ink) or color.ground-2 (4%, the console's sides); an object on it is color.face, the page tone; a small set-back object is color.fill; the edge is surface.edge. Warm is not a surface.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The edge is what makes an object: a card, an input, a library entry. A ground never takes one.

panel-border.$description: FORMER NAME, kept for production's console.css only: now --edge. Nothing in handoff/ may use it; remove once production reads the new name.

tray.$description: The recess a choice sits in: .pills.tray and .seg (decided 2026-10-14). On paper the ground tone since 2026-10-15; a raised band restates a wash of shadow, and a dark band darkens. The chosen option rises out of it as a --face tile.

$extensions.pi.rationale: var(--panel) at the root (2026-10-15, Matt: the 6% shadow wash read as grey). A raised band is already the panel, so .surface--raised restates rgba(var(--sh), .06); the dark-band block keeps .34. --wash-2 could not do this job: it lightens on a dark band, which sank the chosen tile into a raised tray.

scrim.$description: What a modal dialog dims the page with (2026-10-15): the shadow's ink at a third, so the page stays legible behind it.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Added with the console's dialogs (Pl. 08). Built on --sh like the elevations, so it is the same warm shadow, not a neutral black.

pi.options.hairline: DEFAULT. No fill and no shadow, a pure drawn line. Reads cleanest and frees the warm tone to mean something.
pi.options.warm: #F3EFE7 applied to every raised surface. Kept for comparison, but as a global treatment it spends the warm tone on ambience.
pi.options.wash: color-mix(--ink 4%, --bg) light / 5% dark. Neutral, tracks the theme, loses the temperature.

$extensions.pi.decision: 2026-09-24, revised. ONE RAISED SURFACE, NO SWITCH. Hairline, wash and warm were never alternatives to each other: a hairline is an EDGE, a wash is a FACE, warm is an EXCEPTION. A raised surface wants an edge and a face, so --panel is a hairline plus a wash of two percent ink (three until 2026-09-25) — lighter than the wash option was. Cards come in opaque (--panel-face) and sheer (--panel-sheer); pick by what is behind the card, and always opaque over the dashed grid. WARM HAS THREE USES AND NO OTHERS: callouts, violators, and the gradient fields which are built from it. It is not a card or band background.
$extensions.pi.history: The hairline / warm / wash options recorded under pi.options were the 2026-09-24 comparison. All three were folded into the one treatment above; none is a live switch.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The July warm tone, retained as a NAMED EMPHASIS SURFACE rather than the default. Applied with .warm on a component or .surface--warm on a band. This is what the tone became when hairline took over: it stopped being ambience and started meaning something.
$extensions.pi.constraint: THREE USES AND NO FOURTH: callouts, violators, and the gradient-field ramp where it is the paper tone at one step of ink rather than the chroma. Not a card background, not a band fill. .surface--warm was removed on 2026-09-25. If two warm things are visible at once, something is over-emphasised.

warm-border.$description: The edge of a warm callout or violator: transparent, because warm separates by tone.

texture.$description: The dashed grid, applied to regions with .textured and always masked so it fades before any edge. USE IT FREELY (2026-10-15; it was rationed): as many sections as a page wants, but TWO TEXTURED SECTIONS NEVER TOUCH. Put a plain band between them.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Anything sitting on a textured region must be OPAQUE. A translucent card shows dashes through its own face and reads as dirt rather than depth.
$extensions.pi.fade: Every texture fades out — a vignette mask, a band mask, or an algorithmic falloff. A hard-edged rectangle of grid reads as a panel somebody forgot to style; the same texture with dissolved edges reads as atmosphere, and the difference is one line of mask-image. Texture also never goes on top of imagery: two textures in one rectangle read as a screen door.

dither-cell.$description: One dither cell for the whole brand, in CSS pixels per canvas pixel.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Added 2026-09-25, corrected the same day. Every dithered thing on the site is the same 8x8 Bayer matrix — the clips, the gradient fields, the rendered grid, the .mo-resolve overlay — and until now they rendered at different scales, so they read as three effects that happen to look similar rather than one treatment. THREE IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN: a tolerance-quantised run-length histogram of decoded frames from hero-dove.mp4 (720x544) and hero-glass.mp4 (672x560) gives a modal run of TWO SOURCE PIXELS, and those masters are drawn across a 1120px stage, which is 3.1 CSS pixels on screen. Everything derived from them had been running at 1.6 to 2, so the system was about half as coarse as the brand's own assets. The originals were copied into media/ as veil-dove.mp4 and veil-glass.mp4 rather than re-derived, because the asset is the specification.
$extensions.pi.constraint: A live field is held to a pixel budget of 140,000 per frame and its cell steps UP until it fits, so a 100vh live field renders coarser than the token. That is the guardrail, not a bug. Video cells are set by the master's resolution against its drawn width, so the encode widths in the media recipe are what keep the clips near this number.

gridink.$description: The light-page grid by name, so a light band on a dark page can ask for it back. --grid is whichever lattice the current surface wants: --gridink on light, --gridinv on dark.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Added 2026-10-09. Before it, a .surface--invert band on a dark page inherited the white lattice and showed no grid at all.

$extensions.pi.constraint: All motion assets share one treatment: medium cell, 7% mono Bayer dither, greyscale, multiply blend (screen on dark surfaces). That treatment is the brand's image language; an undithered asset will look imported.
$extensions.pi.nonWhiteFootage: Footage shot against white composites onto the page with a multiply blend and the ground disappears. Footage that fills its frame has no white to blend away and stays a grey rectangle. Map its luminance through a seven-stop brand ramp instead, ordered BY LUMINANCE rather than by declaration index so one ramp is correct in both themes. SHIP A CONTINUOUS-TONE GREYSCALE MASTER and map AND dither it at runtime: mapping a pre-dithered master gives only seven input levels, and nearest-level rounding collapses the highlights (the sun in the war clip disappeared into the sky). On dark, a SUBJECT on a seamless reverses the ramp so its ground becomes the page, and a SCENE compresses the ramp so it never reaches the paper tone. Exploration, Pl. 14.
$extensions.pi.placement: ADDED 2026-09-25. A clip WITHOUT a white ground goes edge to edge or not at all. A veil (a subject on a seamless) can sit anywhere, because multiply erases the ground and it has no edges. A mapped scene is a rectangle, and a rectangle of treated video set into a column reads as an imported asset however well it is mapped; full-bleed it reads as the page itself.
$extensions.pi.chroma: ADDED 2026-09-25. The LIGHT ramp is monochrome, paper to ink. Folding the accent through its middle stops made every treated clip the largest chroma-carrying object on its page, which is the opposite of an institutional register. The DARK ramp keeps its warmth deliberately: on near-black it reads as thermal imaging, and on the reversed subject ramp the dove reads as infrared. That is the one place the treatment is allowed to be a picture.
$extensions.pi.cost: Measured 2026-09-24. One clip mapped at runtime holds 121fps, indistinguishable from an empty page; the mapping pass is 1.3ms per frame at 12fps, about 1.5% of one core. The cost is COMPOSITING THE UPSCALED FRAMES, not decode and not the mapping: switching the mapping off while three clips play changes nothing, and setting those same three to visibility:hidden while they keep playing restores full frame rate. So the constraint is how much treated moving picture is PAINTED in one viewport. One clip per page is free.
